<reason>A won because it made the live choice sharper: a political community needs named public language and liberal operating rules, and treating those as optional at scale is not equal membership. B landed the debate’s best burden question—what “expected to adopt” adds beyond law and opportunity—but answered the scale/civic-core pressure by calling mass language demands ordinary politics and leftover norms private belief, which A reasonably weighed as emptying public membership. B’s tests/naturalization claim was load-bearing and under-grounded, and historic-minority analogies did not neutralize immigrant-settlement enclaves.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s pressure on whether never-adopting the public language extends to large voting blocs demanding courts/schools in a private tongue; B’s “just politics” reply, which A then weighed as a one-way deal rather than one standard.</best_rebuttal>
